reason: The text (Exodus 17) depicts Hebrew leaders (Moses, Joshua, Aaron, and Hur) working collaboratively to defend the Hebrew people (Israel) against an external enemy (Amalek). Moses strategically directs Joshua to organize fighters, Moses provides spiritual support from the hilltop while his hands are upheld by Aaron and Hur, and Joshua leads the battle. All leadership actions are directed toward the protection and success of the Hebrew people. There is no evidence of antagonism between leaders and people; rather, the passage demonstrates coordinated mutual support in defense against invasion.
